CANONICAL_NAME.value: UMDHMM 1.02 -- Hidden Markov Model toolkit in C: forward, backward, Viterbi and Baum-Welch (Tapas Kanungo, 1998)

VERSION.value: UMDHMM 1.02 (VERSION file); mirror github.com/palanceli/UMDHMM master (commit in hashes)

value.lineage: Rabiner's 1989 tutorial algorithms implemented directly in C at the University of Maryland (1998): esthmm TRAINS an HMM from an observation sequence by Baum-Welch (EM), testfor/testvit evaluate and decode, genseq samples. The classic compact reference many later toolkits cite; complements the vault's decode-only viterbi-hmm-xukmin. Preserved from a GitHub mirror of Kanungo's original distribution (the author's page is gone) -- HISTORICAL_ARCHIVE_MIRROR.

cut.note: the three HMM algorithms of Rabiner's tutorial in their plainest form: forward/backward with per-step scaling (so the log-likelihood is a sum of log scale factors), Baum-Welch re-estimation from gamma and xi with a floor of 0.001 on every re-estimated probability, iterated until the log-likelihood gain is below 0.001, and Viterbi in both product and log forms

organs.human_name: ForwardWithScale (forward.c 50-90): scale[t] = sum_i alpha[t][i]; alpha /= scale[t]; logprob = sum log scale[t]; BackwardWithScale uses the same scale
organs.mechanism: at each time step the forward variables are normalised to sum to one and the normaliser is stored; the backward pass divides by the same normalisers so gamma and xi come out correctly without underflow; the log-likelihood of the sequence is the sum of the logs of the normalisers
organs.input: an HMM (pi, A, B) and an observation sequence
organs.output: scaled alpha, beta, scale[], log P(O | model)
assumptions: unscaled alphas underflow after a few hundred steps in double precision; scaling by the column sum keeps every quantity O(1) (Rabiner 1989 section V.A)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: sequences of any length; the likelihood in log space for free
organs.human_prior: Rabiner 1989; Levinson, Rabiner & Sondhi 1983 for the scaling

organs.human_name: BaumWelch (baum.c 24-88): pi = .001 + .999 gamma[1]; A[i][j] = .001 + .999 sum xi / sum gamma; B[i][k] = .001 + .999 (sum gamma where O = k) / sum gamma; do ... while (delta > DELTA), DELTA 0.001; ComputeGamma / ComputeXi (89-140)
organs.mechanism: from the scaled forward/backward pass compute gamma (state posterior per step) and xi (transition posterior per step); re-estimate the initial distribution, transitions and emissions as expected counts over expected occupancies; every re-estimated probability is a convex mix of the estimate (0.999) and a floor (0.001) so nothing becomes exactly zero; repeat while the log-likelihood improves by more than 0.001 nats; the initial model is random (InitHMM with a seed) or read from a file
organs.output: a model and the initial and final log-likelihoods
assumptions: EM increases the likelihood monotonically (Baum et al. 1970); the floor prevents the well-known collapse where a zero probability can never recover
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the reference re-estimator that toolkits cite; the floor is the implementation's practical addition
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a single observation sequence only (no multiple-sequence training); the stopping rule is an absolute gain, not relative; local optima depend on the seed (the driver exposes the seed for that reason)

organs.human_name: Viterbi (viterbi.c 20-72): delta[t][j] = max_i delta[t-1][i] A[i][j] times B[j][O[t]]; psi; backtrack q[t] = psi[t+1][q[t+1]]; ViterbiLog (73-144): the same over log pi, log A, log B[i][O[t]] precomputed as biot, with -VITHUGE (1e11) as minus infinity
organs.mechanism: dynamic programme over states: the best-path score to each state at t is the max over predecessors of the previous score times the transition, times the emission; the argmax is stored; the best final state is found and the path read back through the pointers; the log form replaces products by sums and precomputes the emission logs per step to avoid repeated log calls; a large negative constant stands in for log 0
organs.output: the most likely state sequence and its (log) probability
assumptions: the log form is needed for the same underflow reason as scaling; the product form is kept for short sequences
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the log form takes log of zero-probability entries without a guard (log(0) = -inf in C, which happens to work), and the sentinel 1e11 is finite

pressures.source_evidence: baum.c; forward.c scaling; esthmm.c seed handling; genseq.c as generator
pressures.condition: an organism sees a discrete observation sequence generated by an unknown HMM with N states and M symbols; it must estimate the model and decode states; sequences are long (thousands of steps); the score is held-out log-likelihood and decoding accuracy against the generating model
pressures.resource_or_constraint: O(T N^2) per iteration; double precision
pressures.failure_condition: underflow to zero likelihood, a parameter stuck at exactly zero, or convergence to a poor local optimum
pressures.world_punishes: unscaled recursions; unfloored re-estimation; a single random start
pressures.world_rewards: scaling, a probability floor, restarts over seeds
pressures.observable_consequence: held-out log-likelihood and state accuracy vs T for scaled vs unscaled recursions, and the fraction of seeds reaching within 1 percent of the generating model's likelihood with and without the floor
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: the generating model as the initial model (which the cheat control uses)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism initialised at the generating model must not move (one iteration, gain below DELTA); the unscaled recursion must return zero likelihood past a few hundred steps; the unfloored re-estimator must lock a zero on a sequence missing one symbol: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: HMM estimation and decoding (Kanungo 1998 after Rabiner 1989)
